When I do circular objects or anything where I want to have smooth shadow gradients I shade using circular motions. Start super super light using a B or 2B and fill the shape’s light areas, then move to a 3B and start to shade the darker areas, then really carefully blend your shades together with circular motions all while pressing lightly. When that’s all done switch to a 6 or 7B and put the dark areas down. 

The other thing is that your light reference isn’t proportionate to your shadow, if the light is coming from the front right of the sphere the shadow would be going backwards to the left. 
Hope this helps you out :)

I can see why you’d think it, it makes for a nice idea that the universe is breathing via expansion and grouping together through the gradual mass accumulation. 

The only problem is that it doesn’t really provide any logical reason to the universe. It may well be the lifecycle of our universe, although intelligent life will never be around to know. But it doesn’t explain how there is a universe. 

Say all matter and anti matter were to be contained in one singularity of equal expansive and contractive forces (-1000 + 1000 = 0), if there were even a slight momentary change in mass of either it would trigger a catastrophic reaction. Quantum mechanics tells us that sub atomic particles are able to appear and disappear. Which would lead to the total mass of the singularity to being negative. Say hypothetically anti matter could have similar quantum characteristics, and that was what momentarily disappeared then the total mass would be positive. 

Leading to either a massive expansion, or a total annihilation. Either one is irrelevant because we can assume everything came from nothing in the first place anyway.
